title: Block One Anchor, Ras Finds Another

scenes.tts: If Ras must carry a farnesyl chain to work, block the enzyme that attaches it. That was the idea behind farnesyl transferase inhibitors. Ras genes are mutated in roughly one in five human cancers. A Ras that cannot reach the membrane cannot signal.
scenes.caption: If Ras must carry a farnesyl chain to work, block the enzyme that attaches it. That was the idea behind farnesyltransferase inhibitors. Ras genes are mutated in roughly one in five human cancers. A Ras that cannot reach the membrane cannot signal.
scenes.visual: If Ras must carry a farnesyl chain: a Ras held on the membrane by its farnesyl chain. A second Ras waits in the cytosol while an enzyme would add its chain; a drug blocks the enzyme and the chain slot stays empty. Five tiles, one filled, mark one in five cancers. The blocked Ras stays low and cannot signal.
scenes.narration: If Ras must carry a farnesyl chain to work, block the enzyme that attaches it. That was the idea behind farnesyltransferase inhibitors. Ras genes are mutated in roughly one in five human cancers. A Ras that cannot reach the membrane cannot signal.

scenes.tts: One of these drugs, tipifarnib, reached Phase three clinical trials. The drugs worked as drugs. Yet they still disappointed against the Ras that matters most. K Ras is by far the most commonly mutated of the three Ras genes. H Ras is the least.
scenes.caption: One of these drugs, tipifarnib, reached Phase III clinical trials. The drugs worked as drugs. Yet they still disappointed against the Ras that matters most. K-Ras is by far the most commonly mutated of the three Ras genes. H-Ras is the least.
scenes.visual: A class chip for the farnesyltransferase inhibitors, with tipifarnib and a Phase III badge as one of them. The drugs worked as drugs, then disappointed against the Ras that matters most. K-Ras and H-Ras blobs are labelled most and least mutated; N-Ras sits apart, unranked.
scenes.narration: One of these drugs, tipifarnib, reached Phase III clinical trials. The drugs worked as drugs. Yet they still disappointed against the Ras that matters most. K-Ras is by far the most commonly mutated of the three Ras genes. H-Ras is the least.

scenes.tts: Here is the catch. When farnesylation is blocked, K Ras and N Ras can be picked up by a second enzyme. It is geranylgeranyl transferase one. It puts a geranylgeranyl group, a longer chain, on the same cysteine. The protein keeps its anchor, and keeps signaling.
scenes.caption: Here is the catch. When farnesylation is blocked, K-Ras and N-Ras can be picked up by a second enzyme. It is geranylgeranyltransferase I. It puts a geranylgeranyl group, a longer chain, on the same cysteine. The protein keeps its anchor, and keeps signaling.
scenes.visual: K-Ras and N-Ras wait low, the farnesyl enzyme blocked by the drug. A second enzyme links to both, a longer chain grows on the same spot marked as the cysteine, both proteins rise to the membrane and signal.
scenes.narration: Here is the catch. When farnesylation is blocked, K-Ras and N-Ras can be picked up by a second enzyme. It is geranylgeranyltransferase I. It puts a geranylgeranyl group, a longer chain, on the same cysteine. The protein keeps its anchor, and keeps signaling.

scenes.tts: H Ras is not rescued this way. The logic has not died. Tipifarnib has been tested in cancers driven by mutant H Ras. So keep this rule: block farnesyl, and K Ras and N Ras can switch anchors, but H Ras cannot.
scenes.caption: H-Ras is not rescued this way. The logic has not died. Tipifarnib has been tested in cancers driven by mutant H-Ras. So keep this rule: block farnesyl, and K-Ras and N-Ras can switch anchors, but H-Ras cannot.
scenes.visual: H-Ras waits low; the second enzyme comes and is turned away, so H-Ras is not rescued. A tipifarnib chip points at a label for cancers driven by mutant H-Ras. The rule appears in two lines.
scenes.narration: H-Ras is not rescued this way. The logic has not died. Tipifarnib has been tested in cancers driven by mutant H-Ras. So keep this rule: block farnesyl, and K-Ras and N-Ras can switch anchors, but H-Ras cannot.
